03

Printed Studies

A printed study for a named developer, builder or land owner: what the firm could build in print, the machine, how a printed wall handles weather, heat and moisture, the math and the next step. The Fit tab lists what printing adds for a firm of its type, each with a published figure, and where it applies in the firm's own projects.

06

Bedrock

Bedrock is where the guidelines behind these tools are gathered, so each deliverable can be produced again, the same way, for any firm. It holds the page components, the rules for copy, sourcing and figures, and one register with the wording for every fact that more than one tool states.

Archivo, two weights
IBM Plex Mono
labels, data, sources
  • Figures, checked against the bytes of each cited page
  • Links, checked for status and banned hosts
  • Copy, checked against a list of banned words and em dashes
  • Every view opened at phone and desktop width, in both themes
Bedrock component sheet

Four of the rules, with their sources

Compare by position on a common scale: bars, dots and ranges, not pies or bubbles.

Cleveland and McGill, 1984

A figure's title says what is drawn. The finding goes in the reading under it.

Kong, Liu and Karahalios, 2018

A strip of about four numbers, a view of four or five steps.

Cowan, 2001

No mono text under 11px, no reading text under 12.5px.

Legge and Bigelow, 2011
